Lights Out — solvable by construction, and why that matters

How NoCharge Lights Out creates a solvable five-by-five board with 13 seeded cross toggles, and what its in-session move count does not claim.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Turn every light off with five-cell toggles.

Play Lights OutBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Lights Out starts from an all-off five-by-five board and applies 13 deterministic, seeded cross-shaped toggles. Repeating those toggles reverses the scramble, so a solution exists by construction.

What one press changes

Pressing a square toggles that square and its orthogonal neighbors—up, down, left, and right—when those neighbors are inside the board. Diagonal squares are not changed. A corner press therefore affects fewer squares than a press in the center.

How the starting board is made

The generator starts with 25 lights off. A seeded linear-congruential sequence chooses 13 press positions, and the game applies those presses to build the initial board. Some chosen positions may repeat; pressing the same cross twice cancels its effect. The final lit-cell count can therefore be smaller than 13.

Because each toggle is its own inverse, applying the same 13 presses again would return the board to all off. That proves at least one solution exists; it does not prove the puzzle is easy, that the shortest solution has 13 moves, or that the solution is unique.

What the move display records

The move count increases for each press in the active board. It is an in-session counter, not a saved personal best or a ranking. New puzzle advances to the next deterministic seed; the reset/runtime initialization returns to the first seed. No score history is stored in NoCharge V2.

For a practical session, inspect the cross affected by each candidate press and remember that pressing it twice cancels it. The current game page states the controls and displays the five-by-five board.
